author: Sofía Oillataguerre
title: A la sombra del paraíso: entre flores y mandatos
content:
A la sombra del paraíso; escrita e interpretada por Marcela De Grande


Ambientada en un vivero durante el día de San Valentín, la obra sigue a una mujer que intenta sostener sola el negocio familiar mientras espera una ayuda que nunca llega. Desde esa premisa, despliega una mirada sobre los vínculos, los cuidados y el amor romántico.

Por Sofía Oillataguerre (ANRed)


A la sombra del paraíso

 es un unipersonal, interpretado por la gran actuación de

Marcela De Grande

, con una puesta en escena detallista y delicada que recrea con sensibilidad el universo de un vivero.


La obra parece partir de una aceptación del imaginario del amor romántico, blanco y heterosexual. Su protagonista, madre y esposa, queda sola al frente del vivero en el día de mayor demanda del año: San Valentín. Mientras espera a su hijo adolescente que nunca llega a ayudarla, recibe la llamada de su marido, quien le anuncia sin previo diálogo, que se va de la casa.


A partir de allí, ella intenta sostener el trabajo, contener su angustia y seguir adelante. Su dolor queda desplazado por los mensajes de amor que escribe para los clientes que compran flores para sus parejas. Desde el comienzo, la propia protagonista señala con cierta lucidez que

«se acuerdan de las flores solo este día»

, una observación que deja entrever una mirada sobre los rituales románticos.


Sin embargo, la obra elige no profundizar en una crítica de esos valores tradicionales, sino narrarlos desde la experiencia de su protagonista. Esa decisión abre algunas preguntas para quienes miramos la historia desde otro lugar: ¿qué sucede con las mujeres que sostienen, casi sin fisuras, el mandato de madre abnegada, esposa complaciente y trabajadora incansable? ¿Hay espacio para cuestionar ese modelo o simplemente se lo representa?


Es, desde luego, una lectura personal. La función fue a sala llena, las risas acompañaron gran parte del recorrido y la obra permanece en cartel desde febrero, señales de una propuesta que claramente encuentra resonancia en sus espectadores.


A la sombra del paraíso puede verse los viernes a las 21 h en El Camarín de las Musas, Mario Bravo 960. Entradas

author: Mada Masr
title: Fire at Damietta Port energy facilities brought under control, says Petroleum Ministry, without comment on cause
content:
A fire broke out at natural gas facilities in the Damietta Port on Wednesday afternoon, the Petroleum Ministry said in a

statement

, without elaborating on the cause of the incident. 


Maritime security firm

Ambrey


said

 that a drone struck a United States-owned LNG floating storage facility and a Greek-owned LNG tanker at the port, causing a fire that the security firm said was brought under control. 


The Petroleum Ministry affirmed in its statement that there were no injuries or fatalities as a result of the fire, urging media outlets and social media users to refer to official statements issued by the ministry for further information. 


The ministry said that the fire had broken out on a regasification vessel and a storage vessel in the port. 


Damietta is a key energy logistics site, hosting natural gas facilities that serve Egypt’s export and import needs.  


Regasification and storage vessels are currently stationed in its port to facilitate Egypt’s use of imported energy cargo to power homes and industries across the country. 


Reuters

cited

 trade sources to report that the vessel that had been struck is Energos Winter, a storage and regasification unit that sails

under

 a Marshall Islands flag that was

contracted

 by Egypt’s government to Damietta Port last year to support Egypt’s gas import processing.


The trade sources and energy sources said the cause of the fire was a drone strike.


Egypt’s logistics and energy facilities had not been targeted so far, though similar sites on both sides of the Persian Gulf have become frequent targets over recent months in the war that the United States and Israel launched against Iran.


While fire has calmed amid ongoing ceasefire negotiations, more attacks flared Wednesday as the US

said

 that its forces in the region were targeted by Iranian fire.


The US said in turn that it had teamed up with Saudi Arabia to attack armed groups in

Iraq

allied with Iran.

author: David Venn
title: Sealift unloading accident causes power outage in Pangnirtung
content:
This story was updated on Thursday, July 30, at 11:15 a.m. ET


An accident that occurred while offloading from a sealift has left the hamlet office and community hall in Pangnirtung without power and IT services.


On July 24, at around 8:45 p.m., an employee for a sealift operator drove a trailer with a high load near the community hall, where they snagged a power line, said deputy Mayor Markus Wilcke in an interview.


“Two poles were torn down, the cables broke, three transformers hit the road and we actually had some leakage of the transformer liquid as well,” he said.


It’s unclear which shipping company was responsible for the damage.


Initially, the entire community experienced a power outage, Wilcke said.


Within 50 minutes, local crews restored power to an area that included Government of Nunavut offices and the Co-op, according to an emailed statement from the Qulliq Energy Corp.


QEC chartered a flight into Pangnirtung, arriving shortly after midnight. Crews replaced the two power poles and, by 10 a.m. July 25, they restored power for the area that includes the Northern store, RCMP detachment and airport.


An environmental engineer who is visiting the community worked with the shipping company to isolate contamination from the transformer liquid, Wilcke said. Eight cubic metres of contaminated soil was dug up with a backhoe, stored in specialized bags and loaded onto the ship.


“Everybody did actually an amazing job,” he said. “There was excellent teamwork.”


The energy corporation echoed the sentiment.


“QEC also recognizes the dedication and professionalism of its local power plant operators, who responded immediately to the incident, as well as the power line crew dispatched from Iqaluit, whose swift efforts enabled power to be restored safely to the community,” the email from QEC said.


But the hamlet office and community hall, which are located in the same building, are still mostly offline because the cables were “literally torn out of the fuse panel,” Wilcke said.


Despite the damage, the finance department managed to finish payroll, which “was kind of considered an emergency,” Wilcke said, “because people like to get paid — on time.”


The hamlet was still waiting as of Wednesday for out-of-town electricians to assess the damage, for Northwestel to restore the phone and internet lines and for QEC to connect the buildings to the electrical poles, Wilcke said.


The community hall remained closed, and all events scheduled to take place there have been cancelled or postponed.


Wilcke said he expects everything to be fixed early next week.


In an emailed statement, he said he isn’t sure how much this incident will cost, but that it “is expected to be substantial.”


Clarification:

 This story has been updated to remove the name of a shipping company that was in Pangnirtung July 22 through 24, because more than one sealift was scheduled to be in Pangnirtung’s port on the date of the incident.

author: anred
title: El peso de la vida: en 10 años se duplicaron los suicidios y hay un suicidio adolescente por día
content:
Los suicidios triplican a los homicidios. La media argentina supera en 2.7 a la mundial. En ese marco, cada día un adolescente entre los 10 y los 19 años se quita la vida. Por cada caso letal hay hasta 20 intentos. Entre las causas, historias de sextorsión, deudas por apuestas y profundas soledades, mientras crece la vida en las redes. Mientras, en los hospitales nacionales de salud mental, el gobierno recortó el presupuesto en un 44%. «Suicidarse no es un objetivo sino una estrategia. Y esto lo considero importante para evaluar políticas de prevención del suicidio. El suicidio es un mal. Pero no es un absoluto mal. El absoluto mal es todo aquello que lleva a considerar el suicidio como una estrategia», señala Alfredo Grande, psiquiatra, referente del Psicoanalisis implicado y la Clínica Social, y presidente de la cooperativa de trabajo en salud mental ATICO.

Por Claudia Rafael, Silvana Melo y Alfredo Grande, para Agencia Pelota de Trapo.


El peso de la vida: en diez años se duplicaron los suicidios


Esta es la primera parte de un informe sobre el desmesurado crecimiento de los suicidios en el país. Los suicidios triplican a los homicidios. La media argentina supera en 2.7 a la mundial. Mientras se recortan presupuestos en las áreas de salud mental.

Por Claudia Rafael y Silvana Melo.


(APe).-

 La angustia cuando se hace profunda y el mundo cuando se vuelve intolerable desactivan los hilos que sostienen la vida y empieza a ser cotidiana la tentación de arrancársela. 5.209 personas sintieron ese derrumbe durante 2025 y fueron contabilizadas por el Ministerio de Seguridad de la Nación en una gélida columna de 

muertes violentas

. Cuando en realidad eran suicidios. Que no tenían nada que ver con los homicidios ni con los accidentes. Esa demolición de la voluntad que empuja a terminar con la vida aumentó un 22,6% en la Argentina solamente en un año: entre 2024 y 2025.


No es casual en una docena de meses cuando la miserabilidad desde el poder agudizó la carencia de los más castigados y los culpó de su desgracia.


El informe de Estadística Criminal que el Ministerio de Seguridad dio a conocer en celebración de una baja del 7,1 por ciento en los homicidios dolosos, exhibe también una cifra de diez años escalofriante que, sin embargo, no mereció ninguna reacción oficial: desde 2016 hasta el 2025 la cifra de suicidios aumentó un 79,80 %.  En una década la subsistencia de muchos argentinos entró en una espiral de disvalor que casi duplicó a quienes decidieron terminar con su vida.


En esos diez años, 38.283 personas se quitaron la vida. Algo así como la desaparición de toda la población de ciudades como Bell Ville, Funes, Lobos o Chascomús. El 13,60 % de ese total ocurrió en 2025. El año con el mayor número de suicidios a lo largo de toda la historia. Hasta ahora.


La tasa nacional trepó a 11,8 casos cada 100.000 habitantes, mientras que el promedio mundial que informa la Organización Mundial de la Salud es de 9,1. Provincias como Entre Ríos, que suele perforar todos los extremos, llega al 20,8.


En apenas un año, los suicidios en la provincia de Buenos Aires aumentaron un 55,4%. En CABA, un 38,3%. En Misiones, un 36,93%. En Salta, un 34,6%. En Santa Cruz, un 33,4%. Cada distrito con sus particulares hostilidades hacia diferentes grupos sociales. Buenos Aires abarca un nivel de hacinamiento, disparidad social, pauperización y migración laboral que logra ganar varios premios en frustraciones, precarización, desempleo y pobreza. Una desvalorización de la vida propia que tiende a desencarnarse.


Inseguridades: e

l suicidio triplica a los homicidios dolosos


Los gobiernos suelen desplegar discursos, planteos y plataformas grandilocuentes contra la violencia y la inseguridad. Pero sus propias estadísticas denuncian que la gente a la que deben representar se mata tres veces más de lo que la matan. Pero para esta tragedia no hay plataformas ni discursos ni programas preventivos. Se desfinancian los dispositivos de salud mental. Y se deja más sola a la gente que necesita escucha y compañía. Se profundiza el silencio y las emociones no nombradas. Nombrar el suicidio, dicen desde la psicología, “no es promoverlo, sino desarmar los silencios que lo rodean”.


Rastrear las razones de ese incremento estremecedor es, de alguna manera, una radiografía social de cómo se vive, de las angustias que superan la vara de lo soportable y de las soledades que atraviesan a una porción creciente de la población. Que en un país como …

author: Tom Midlane
title: US Private Equity Firm Takes Control of NHS Patient Records
content:
A US private equity firm is set to take control of NHS patient records, sparking further concerns about Britain’s public bodies handing over sensitive personal data to private firms. 


Asset management company TPG acquired healthcare technology business Optum UK earlier this year in a £300m deal that included subsidiary


EMIS – the firm that supplies the IT and patient records system used by most GPs in England.


“The GP records of more than half the country sit on a system controlled by a firm whose business model is returns for investors, not care for patients, and the public found out after the fact,” a spokesperson for campaign group Doctors’ Association UK (DAUK)

told the Guardian

. 


The spokesperson compared the move to spytech giant Palantir’s incursion into the NHS and called for the government to set out what safeguards are in place. 


An investigation by the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ)

alleged that TPG-backed firm Evercare

 had driven patients in Kenya deeper into poverty and debt, with some even asked to hand over land deeds to cover unpaid medical bills.


A TPG spokesperson told the Guardian the company strongly disagreed “with the facts and characterisation of the allegations in the ICIJ’s report” and said its investments in Evercare had led to “substantial gains in quality, accessibility, and accreditations, as well as patient rights and protections.”


“Any suggestion that TPG or Evercare prioritises profits over patients is incorrect and ignores the extensive clinical governance and patient’s rights policies we’ve instituted,” they added.


 

Former Oxfam health policy lead Anna Marriott told the Guardian: “It is deeply concerning that a private equity firm with a highly controversial track record in healthcare internationally can take control of sensitive NHS patient data with so little public scrutiny.


“This deal should ring major alarm bells. Private equity’s penetration of our health service is fast outrunning the regulatory guardrails needed to protect patients, workers and the public interest.”


EMIS said “patient privacy” and “rigorous controls” were “core” to its practices and that the acquisition will have no impact on patient privacy. TPG said: “Assertions that TPG could in any way access, control, maintain, or utilise NHS patient records are entirely false.”

author: anred
title: Cierra el Bar Notable Los Laureles: la crisis económica también golpea al patrimonio cultural porteño
content:
El histórico Bar Notable Los Laureles, ubicado en Barracas y fundado en 1893, anunció el cierre definitivo de sus puertas. La noticia fue comunicada por quienes gestionaron el espacio durante los últimos cuatro años mediante un sentido mensaje en el que expresan el «profundo dolor» de tener que bajar la persiana de un lugar que definen como «mucho más que un bar».

Por ANRed


La despedida no es solamente la de un comercio. Con el cierre de Los Laureles desaparece uno de los espacios emblemáticos de la cultura popular porteña, reconocido como Bar Notable de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires y escenario permanente de milongas, orquestas, cantantes y espectáculos de tango que mantuvieron viva una tradición centenaria.


«Los Laureles es historia, identidad, encuentros, abrazos, música, tango, risas, amigos y recuerdos imborrables», señalaron en el comunicado, donde también afirmaron que las razones que motivan el cierre son «diversas y profundamente dolorosas» y que hasta el último día hicieron «todo nuestro esfuerzo para sostener este proyecto con la dignidad y el respeto que un lugar tan emblemático merece».


La noticia se inscribe en un contexto de profunda crisis económica que afecta de manera creciente al sector cultural. La caída del consumo, el incremento de los costos de funcionamiento y las dificultades para sostener emprendimientos independientes impactan de lleno sobre espacios que cumplen una función social, artística y patrimonial.


 


Cada cierre de un ámbito de estas características implica mucho más que la pérdida de una fuente de trabajo. También desaparece un escenario para artistas, músicos, bailarines, trabajadores de la gastronomía y técnicos; un lugar de encuentro para vecinos y vecinas; y un espacio donde el patrimonio cultural deja de ser una pieza de museo para convertirse en una experiencia cotidiana.


En los últimos meses, teatros, centros culturales, librerías, salas de música y espacios independientes vienen advirtiendo sobre las dificultades para sostener sus actividades. El cierre de Los Laureles se suma a esa preocupación y pone de relieve el deterioro de un entramado cultural construido durante décadas, cuya continuidad depende tanto del esfuerzo de quienes lo gestionan como de políticas públicas que lo protejan.


La pérdida resulta especialmente significativa por tratarse de un Bar Notable con más de 130 años de historia. No alcanza con declarar patrimonio a un edificio si las condiciones económicas terminan expulsando los proyectos culturales que le dan vida. La preservación del patrimonio no se limita a conservar una fachada: supone garantizar que esos espacios continúen siendo lugares de producción artística, memoria colectiva y encuentro comunitario.


«Los Laureles cerrará sus puertas, pero nadie podrá cerrar los recuerdos que vivimos entre estas paredes», concluye el comunicado. Sin embargo, detrás de esa despedida queda una advertencia: cuando la crisis obliga a cerrar espacios culturales históricos, no solo pierde un barrio. Pierde también la memoria viva de una ciudad.

author: anred
title: El agronegocio lo hizo: epidemia de abortos espontáneos e hipotiroidismo en ciudades con uso de agrotóxicos
content:
Foto: Nicolás Pousthomis – Minga/ Agencia Tierra Viva


Nueve pueblos dedicados al agro transgénico y el aumento alarmante de embarazos que no llegan a término y de casos de hipotiroidismo. Un trabajo científico único en su tipo demostró el impacto sanitario de los agrotóxicos en las mujeres de regiones fumigadas. A tres décadas de agronegocio en Argentina, las pruebas son contundentes y solo los cómplices pueden negar las consecuencias del modelo agropecuario.

Por Darío Aranda (

Agencia Tierra Viva).


Un nuevo estudio científico confirma el vínculo directo entre el modelo agropecuario, los agrotóxicos y el aumento de abortos espontáneos e hipotiroidismo en nueve localidades de Santa Fe. En base al análisis de diez años y 6.497 casos, los investigadores afirman que las mujeres que viven en lugares dedicado al agro transgénico padecieron más del doble (2,4) de casos de abortos espontáneos en una década. «Es irrebatible lo que producen los plaguicidas en la salud de la población, la evidencia científica es contundente», destacó Facundo Fernández, coautor del paper y parte del Instituto de Salud Socioambiental de la Facultad de Ciencias Médicas de Rosario, espacio colectivo que realizó la investigación.


Acebal, Arteaga, Chabás, Luis Palacios, San Genaro, Sastre, Timbúes, Villa Eloísa y San Jorge. Las ocho primeras cuentan con menos de 6.000 habitantes (San Jorge con 19.000) y todas tienen en común la actividad agropecuaria industrial, en base a semillas transgénicas y uso masivo de agrotóxicos.


Políticos y empresarios señalan el «modelo exitoso» del campo y publicitan las «ganancias» vía exportaciones. Y no consideran el impacto en la salud de la población.


Foto: Instituto de Salud Socioambiental – UNR


Un modelo que enferma


El estudio 

«Abortos espontáneos e hipotiroidismo en poblaciones rurales argentinas rodeadas de cultivos pulverizados con plaguicidas»

, publicado en la 

Revista de Salud Pública de la UNC

, confirma que 

vivir en pequeñas localidades rurales expuestas a plaguicidas agrícolas ha tenido un impacto negativo en la salud reproductiva y endócrina de las mujeres

. La investigación confirmó el riesgo para la salud de la población: las mujeres que viven es esos lugares padecieron altas tasas de abortos espontáneos y de hipotiroidismo (2,4 y 2,5 veces respectivamente) en solo una década.


La investigación, realizada por el Instituto de Salud Socioambiental de la Facultad de Ciencias Médicas de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario, señala que las localidades fueron seleccionadas para el estudio por su intensa actividad agrícola, ya que hasta el 80 por ciento de la superficie son destinadas a la producción de cultivos pulverizados con químicos.


«La expansión del modelo agroindustrial, caracterizado por el uso creciente e intensivo de plaguicidas, particularmente glifosato, impacta negativamente en la salud reproductiva de las comunidades. Este impacto se manifiesta, entre otros indicadores, en el incremento sostenido de abortos espontáneos en el primer trimestre del embarazo», es una de las conclusiones de la investigación.


En la introducción del trabajo se citan otras investigaciones que han demostrado que el ambiente intrauterino es el primer punto de contacto con los contaminantes, ya que ciertas sustancias pueden llegar de la madre al feto en desarrollo a través de la placenta. En las nueve localidades registraron 2.870 embarazos entre 2008 y 2018. Del total, 2.501 (87 por ciento) culminaron en nacimientos y 369 (13 por ciento) en pérdidas gestacionales, de las cuales 285 ocurrieron en el primer trimestre. El estudio evidenció que la tasa de abortos espontáneos en el primer trimestre del embarazo aumentó 2,4 veces en pueblos fumigados entre 2008 y 2018.


«Los plaguicidas pueden generar distintos problemas de salud, la afección de distintos aparatos y sistemas de nuestro cuerpo. El estudio 

confirma el aumento del número de pérdidas de embarazo

 a lo largo de diez años en estas localidades expuestas a plaguicidas», resume Fernández.


En paralelo, la investigación confirmó que la incidencia de hipotiroidismo en estas localidades aumentó 2,5 veces en el mismo período de tiempo. El hipotiroidismo se caracterizado por una reducción de la función de la glándula tiroides y la producción de hormonas vitales para la salud. Como elemento de incidencia directa, destacan un trabajo de la Autoridad Europea de Seguridad Alimentaria (EFSA) donde se alerta que sobre 128 ingredientes de …

author: Augusta Lunardi
title: Máfia do pau-brasil: esquema ilegal alimenta mercado global de violinos
content:
A luz da tarde já entrava pelas janelas quando João Santos caminhou até um cofre de metal numa sala estreita, tomada por pilhas de documentos, em um prédio do Ibama. Girou a fechadura com a naturalidade de quem repete aquele gesto há anos. Do lado de dentro, não havia dinheiro, armas ou joias — apenas dezenas de varetas de pau-brasil, já cortadas e prontas para virar arcos de violino. Amarrados a cada lote, pequenos pedaços de papel traziam nomes de empresas escritos à mão. “Esse material vale milhões de reais; por isso, fica tão escondido”, disse Santos à reportagem da

Agência Pública

.


Santos é analista do Instituto Brasileiro do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Naturais Renováveis (Ibama) e, por questões de segurança, seu nome foi alterado e o local onde trabalha não será identificado. O principal depósito do Ibama, onde estão armazenadas toneladas de pau-brasil apreendidas nos últimos anos, permanece fechado a visitas externas. A reportagem solicitou acesso, mas o órgão negou o pedido, alegando motivos de segurança.


O Ibama conta com apenas 900 agentes responsáveis por proteger o meio ambiente e combater o tráfico de fauna e flora em todo o país. Em 2018, na chamada Operação Dó Ré Mi, um pequeno grupo de fiscais passou a investigar o comércio de madeira avermelhada, considerada há séculos a matéria-prima ideal

para os arcos dos instrumentos de corda

 mais prestigiados do mundo. Três anos depois da Dó Ré Mi, em cooperação com a Polícia Federal (PF), deflagraram-se as operações Ibirapitanga I e II — que ajudariam a desvendar um sofisticado esquema de fraude envolvendo a comercialização do pau-brasil, uma das espécies mais ameaçadas da Mata Atlântica.


A Universidade Federal do Sul da Bahia pesquisa a biodiversidade da Mata Atlântica e mantém coleções de madeira regionais, como o Pau-Brasil


Guaraná: o coração do comércio clandestino


A investigação da Operação Dó Ré Mi começou em Guaraná, distrito do município de Aracruz, no Espírito Santo, a cerca de cem quilômetros de Vitória. Cercada por morros verdes, cafezais e fragmentos remanescentes da Mata Atlântica, a localidade pouco difere de tantas outras comunidades rurais do interior brasileiro. Mas foi ali que fiscais passaram a rastrear toneladas de toras e varetas de pau-brasil extraídas ilegalmente de áreas protegidas e mantidas em depósitos sem documentação ou acobertadas por registros fraudulentos.


Uma única rua de Guaraná concentra algumas das principais empresas de arcos de violino do Brasil: Arcos Brasil, Archets Brasil, Bogen Schaeffer e Horst John & Co. Em meio a casas simples e oficinas discretas, ali se estabeleceu um polo que, nas últimas décadas, passou a fornecer arcos e varetas para músicos, lojas de instrumentos e fabricantes especializados no mundo todo. Ao contrário dos tradicionais ateliês europeus — muitos deles centenários, conduzidos pelas mesmas famílias há gerações —, as empresas de Guaraná surgiram há bem menos tempo. Ainda assim, abocanharam um dos segmentos mais exclusivos da indústria de instrumentos musicais graças a uma vantagem que nenhum concorrente estrangeiro pode alcançar: o acesso ao pau-brasil.


Ameaçado de extinção, o pau-brasil resiste hoje em fragmentos da Mata Atlântica, sobretudo no sul da Bahia e no Rio de Janeiro, com pequenos núcleos também no Rio Grande do Norte, na Paraíba, em Pernambuco, em Alagoas e no Espírito Santo.


Com menos de 5 mil habitantes, o distrito de Guaraná (ES) tem na fabricação de arcos de violino uma de suas principais atividades econômicas


Jacy Almeida de Souza, herdeiro da empresa e das propriedades de Horst John em Guaraná, caminha até a igreja construída após a morte de John, em 1997


Na origem dessa história está Horst Ewald Günther John, conhecido em Guaraná apenas como Horst John. Depois da Segunda Guerra Mundial, o comerciante alemão se estabeleceu no Espírito Santo e passou a atuar na extração e na comercialização de madeira. Nos anos 1970, enxergou uma oportunidade de ir além da exportação da matéria-prima ao começar a enviar jovens da região à Alemanha para aprender, com mestres archetiers, a arte de fabricar arcos para instrumentos de corda. Em 1979, fundou a Horst John & Company e, em poucos anos, Guaraná tornou-se referência internacional.


Após a morte de Horst John, no fim dos anos 1990, antigos colaboradores e herdeiros passaram a disputar o espaço deste mercado pequeno e especializado. Em Guaraná, a reportagem visitou uma propriedade de cerca de três hectares, com …

author: Tom Midlane
title: AI Firms Are Buying up Old Books, Then Scanning and Destroying Them
content:
The world’s biggest AI companies are buying antiquarian books en masse so they can be scanned to train their large language models (LLMs) before being destroyed. 


Anthropic, the company behind Claude AI, has spent tens of millions of dollars acquiring millions of books to feed its demand for human-authored training material,

the Washington Post

 reported earlier this year. 


Under the codename Project Panama, the firm used a hydraulic powered cutting machine to lop off books’ spines and then slice individual pages, which could then be scanned with industrial-grade imaging equipment before being discarded. 


Internal documents unsealed in legal filings in January revealed that Anthropic was acutely aware of how negatively such a project would be received outside the company. 


“Project Panama is our effort to destructively scan all the books in the world,” an internal planning document said. “We don’t want it to be known that we are working on this.”


Earlier this month a judge approved a $1.5bn (£1.1bn) payment in a class action lawsuit brought against Anthropic by a group of authors whose pirated work had been used to train Claude.


However, in the original ruling last year, a judge found that Anthropic’s use of physical books was protected as fair use under US law, Futurism reported. 


The company was able to evade copyright issues by hiding behind a legal rule known as first-sale doctrine, which allows a buyer to do what they want with an item after purchasing.


The doctrine enables the second-hand book trade to exist – and a new market has now sprung up explicitly catering to AI companies seeking to buy vast quantities of old books. 


“I personally have mixed feelings about all of this,” one bookseller told 404 Media. “It benefits me financially as well as by clearing out old inventory that is otherwise unlikely to sell. 


“I’ve been well-suited for these sales with inventory from overseas and foreign language books. On the other hand, I don’t like the end-use, and I don’t like that uncommon books are being pulped.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Apex property to be cleared of garbage and vehicles
content:
A residential property in Apex will be cleared of derelict vehicles and mounds of flammable debris after a tenant’s appeal was unanimously rejected by Iqaluit city councillors on Tuesday night.


Keven Brouillette awaits surgery for a stab wound to the head in Ottawa on Tuesday. He said he’s disappointed Iqaluit city council proceeded with a hearing into his appeal of a clean-up order for his Apex residence. The appeal was rejected. (Photo courtesy of Keven Brouillette)


The residence at 3266 Jack Anawak St. is surrounded by 14 cars in various states of disrepair, more than 70 tires, oil drums, propane tanks and miscellaneous trash.


“The vehicles lined around the house do pose a significant risk to the occupant, the neighbours, as well as fire department personnel,” Iqaluit fire Chief Solomon Tagak said in an email to Steven Allen, Iqaluit’s chief municipal enforcement officer, in late May.


The email was included in a city document package released ahead of the hearing.


City staff reached the home’s owner, Christos Paulidis, on May 29 by cellphone and email, advising of the clean-up order for violations of the Unsightly Land Bylaw.


“I have no idea what they’re doing. I am 83 years old. What are they trying to do — kill me?” Paulidis said, during a phone interview shortly before the hearing.


Paulidis is in hospital in Ottawa, since falling while on vacation two months ago.


Paulidis said he contacted his tenant, Keven Brouillette, and instructed him to clean up the yard before the city’s June 12 deadline.


“I told him to throw all the cars in the garbage and to clean my house,” Paulidis said.


Instead, Brouillette submitted a letter of appeal asking the city for a 90-day extension on the clean-up order, which would have pushed the deadline to Sept. 10.


Low cash flow and lingering ice prevented him from clearing the yard, he told the city.


“I am seeking a reasonable opportunity to address the situation responsibly and effectively while managing the financial and logistical challenges I currently face,” he said in his written appeal.


But then

Brouillette was medevaced to Ottawa on July 23 after being

stabbed

 in the head at a residence in Iqaluit’s Joamie Court neighbourhood. A 28-year-old man is charged with attempted murder in the attack.


Reached by phone from his hospital bed Tuesday, Brouillette said h

e sent a formal request to postpone Tuesday’s appeal hearing and that he was offered the option to attend remotely. This was not possible, Brouillette said, as he was scheduled to be in surgery during the hearing.


He said he is disappointed the city chose to proceed with the hearing without him.


“I don’t understand why they can’t just postpone for me to go defend my point,” he said. “What I was trying to do there is actually just help out the community.”


Brouillette said the vehicles on the property are part of his home-based mobile-mechanic business, Northern Auto Solutions.


The business “wasn’t officially on paper,” he said.


The city considers Brouillette’s business as “an unlicensed mechanic repair shop” located in “an unpermitted constructed garage structure” that straddles the property line, according to city documents. 


Nunatsiaq News contacted the City of Iqaluit to ask why the meeting was not postponed but did not hear back in time for publication. No members of the public attended the meeting and councillors voted after an in-camera discussion.


Bylaw officers have contacted the last known owners of all the cars on the property, based on their vehicle identification numbers.


All costs associated with the cleanup will be incurred by the property owner, as per the bylaw.

author: anonerror
title: Un par de textos en Anarquía
content:
En algún rincón de Buenos Aires, Argentina, en el año 2070 …

Rubén se despierta aturdido en una jaula mugrienta, Huele a hierro oxidado …  y a una mezcla de sudor y detergente, a su lado, un señor con barba mece su perilla, trajeado, luce un reloj retro, no es el tipo de delincuente habitual que frecuentaba las cárceles, al menos no lo era hace 50 años antes de que Argentina se convirtiera en una monarquía absoluta proclamada por Javier Milei, un tipo de minarquía con pretensiones anárquicas de libre mercado, en la que los sucesores de dicho presidente hacían valer su ley del dejar hacer a empresarios de la droga y la prostitución, a bancos que emiten su propia moneda y a corredurías de seguros.

Rubén se dirige al hombre a su lado, algo magullado.

- ¿Quién sos vos, y que hago yo aquí?

- No sufras, parece que esos guardias de la agencia te han pegado una buena tunda – dijo el desconocido - estas en una cárcel propiedad de dicha agencia, una cárcel privada, ¿Puedes recordar tu nombre?

- Sí… me llamo Rubén,  ¡Che, me duele todo! ¿¡Qué ha hecho vos para estar aquí, parece usted un buen hombre, y todo un intelectual?!

- Bueno, fui profesor de Economía en el secundario en Buenos Aires, en un barrio humilde – explica con una mirada triste y una sonrisa amarga, mientras mece una tiza en su mano, sin pesarlo hace una mueca en la pared, es un día más en la celda - Cuando privatizaron la escuela, la nueva dirección decidió que había que establecer salarios a precios de mercado, es decir, bajarnos los sueldos, algunos de nosotros, los profesores, protestamos y nos despidieron,  ¡Acusados de violar la libertad del estudiantado, de fomentar el bullying en las escuelas! La concha de su madre … ¿Te lo puedes creer? Desde entonces no pude mantener mi piso en alquiler y el casero me denunció, el Tribunal de Arbitraje falló a favor de saldar la deuda económica… y aquí me hallo. ¿Qué te paso a vos?

- Apenas recuerdo…  lo último que tengo en mente es ir a mis clases de Medicina, en una academia… EducaSalud.S.A. se llamaba o algo así, mis padres se llaman Ana, una mujer encantadora y mi padre Eduardo; ella es camarera y el, barrendero.

- ¿Sos vos también de barrio humilde, entonces?

-Sí, somos también de barrio pobre, mi barrio no está vallado ni tiene seguridad privada, en mi barrio la criminalidad y los delitos armados aumentan sin parar ¡que desastre, loco!

-Te entiendo… Lo llaman “Conducta desviada… ¡Respecto al principio de no agresión!”.

- Me temo, que para los cínicos en el poder, no significa nada. Te han dado justicia privada de la buena esos pelotudos. Levanta amigo, ha sonado la sirena, nos toca el turno.

-¿Qué turno? – Dijo Rubén desconcertado

-¿Eres nuevo aquí por lo que veo, eh? El turno de los trabajos de reinserción, ¡debemos trabajar gratis hasta saldar nuestra deuda! ¡Empaquetando y embalando!

-Lo que oís, la agencia de seguridad tiene un convenio, un contrato con unos grandes almacenes, es su manera de ganar plata, repercutirá a favor de las cuentas de con quien estés endeudado… Si estás aquí, me temo que acumulas una gran deuda, estimado amigo... Así es…

Rubén se levanta al día siguiente, con su nueva compañía, su compañero de celda al lado. Es su segundo día en la cárcel y le había cogido cariño, había aprendido que se llamaba Enrique. Rubén ya se encontraba mejor…

-Empiezo a recodar mi propia historia… - anunció Rubén

-Dime, Rubén… - dijo expectante Enrique

-¡Fui acusado de cometer una negligencia! Fue en mis primeros días de laburo.

-Bueno… no sé hasta qué punto soy responsable de ello…

author: Mikhail Nyamweya
title: Gen Z and the Realpolitik of Kenya’s 2027 Election
content:
Kenya’s Gen Z has already achieved what many thought impossible. It forced a sitting government into retreat, disrupted the language of national politics, and demonstrated that a decentralized movement could challenge state power without waiting for opposition leaders, ethnic kingpins, or civil society gatekeepers. It made taxation, corruption, police brutality, and public arrogance matters of everyday conversation. A generation dismissed as online, distracted or apolitical instead organized, educated and mobilized with remarkable speed.


But as Kenya moves closer to the 2027 general election, the harder question is whether it can convert protest into political power in an electoral field shaped by an embattled incumbent, a fractured opposition, and a political class with a remarkable ability to absorb anger without necessarily changing. The

 2024 Finance Bill protests

 were a turning point because they were never only about taxation. The bill became the object through which wider frustration found expression. Young people were rejecting a political culture in which citizens are repeatedly asked to make sacrifices while leaders appear insulated from the consequences of their own decisions. The anger was fiscal, but it was also moral. It was about the cost of living, but equally about the cost of being ignored.


This is why the Gen Z moment mattered. It broke the familiar script of Kenyan politics. For decades, national mobilization has often depended on party structures, ethnic blocs, regional brokers and elite bargains. The protests unsettled that order. They were decentralized, digitally coordinated, and issue-based. They did not wait for politicians to speak. Young people named MPs, circulated information, created protest art, translated complex policy into popular language, and turned online outrage into street presence.


In that sense, Gen Z has already won something important. It has changed what counts as political participation. Politics is no longer confined to rallies, party headquarters, parliamentary speeches or election campaigns. It now happens in TikTok explainers, X Spaces, WhatsApp groups, memes, screenshots, civic education threads and viral slogans. A generation once accused of apathy has created a new civic vocabulary.


Yet visibility is not the same as power. Protest legitimacy is not electoral legitimacy. Delegitimizing an incumbent is not the same as constructing a government-in-waiting. Elections reward organization as much as conviction, coalition building as much as moral clarity, and institutional discipline as much as popular enthusiasm. That is the realpolitik now confronting Kenya’s youngest political generation.


Ruto’s politics of survival


President William Ruto appears to understand this distinction better than many of his critics. His political problem is serious, but it is not impossible. He faces the anger of a young population that feels betrayed by the gulf between campaign promises and lived hardship. He faces continuing resentment over taxation, unemployment, corruption, police violence, and the handling of protest. The “one term” slogan captures something real: the desire to punish power.


But Ruto also has advantages that should not be underestimated. He is the incumbent. He has access to state machinery, a national campaign structure, parliamentary networks, administrative reach, and the discipline of someone who has spent years mastering electoral arithmetic. His strategy will not necessarily be to win Gen Z over emotionally. It may be to survive them politically. 


AFCON 2027 may also become part of this survival politics. Kenya will co-host the tournament with Uganda and Tanzania from 19 June to 17 July 2027, just weeks before the general election. On paper, this is a sporting event. Politically, however, it offers the incumbent a rare stage on which to perform infrastructure delivery, regional leadership, national pride, and stability. Stadiums, roads, ceremonies, visiting fans, and the language of East African “

Pamoja

” can easily become part of a broader campaign mood. This does not mean football will determine the election, but it may give the government a symbolic platform through which to shift attention from anger to achievement, from protest to patriotism, and from discontent to spectacle.


That survival strategy is visible in the broader logic of incorporation. In the wake of the protests, Ruto

 nominated opposition figures to his cabinet

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Teacher Arrested for Clapping at Data Centre Meeting in US
content:
A physics teacher was arrested for clapping a speaker who criticised a planned data centre at a public meeting in the US last week.


Lux Claridge was dragged away by police at the meeting in Emporia, Kansas, prompting a plea of “please don’t hurt them” from the resident who had been speaking.


​Attendees at the meeting had been warned to avoid “snapping, clapping” and “rude comments” by mayor Becky Smith, but Claridge insisted he had a right to applaud speakers.


“I have a right to clap… drag me out,” he said.


“Claridge did not comply with law enforcement’s efforts to remove him from the premises, requiring officers to physically carry him out of the meeting,” Emporia police said in a statement.


He was charged with disorderly conduct and interference with law enforcement. He was later released on bail. 


​”I’m glad to be out, but this is an inconvenience, really,” Claridge told the local KWCH news station. “It’s not really deterring me from speaking out or, I guess, clapping.”


His trial is set for September and he plans to plead not guilty. 


​Residents attended the 22 July meeting to oppose the planned Flint Hills Digital Campus data centre. 


Opposition to data centres

has exploded across the US

 in recent months. Grassroots groups blocked 75 projects worth $130bn between 1 January and 31 March 2026, figures from Data Center Watch show. 


The number of anti-data centre groups, meanwhile, has doubled to 833 across 49 states.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: India Unleashes "Massive Crackdown" on Youth-Led Cockroach Movement After Education Minister's Ouster
content:
We go to New Delhi for an update on India’s youth-led, anti-government “Cockroach” movement. After weeks of street protests against Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the ruling

BJP

 party, Pradhan tendered his resignation on Saturday. Now, however, protest leaders are accusing right-wing Prime Minister Narendra Modi of reneging on his promise to not take punitive action against demonstrators. “Because this government and its policy is, and has always been, that of vengeance, … we are witnessing a massive crackdown on student activists across the country,” says Neha Bora, a doctoral student at Jawaharlal Nehru University and the national president of the All India Students Association. Bora spent 23 days on hunger strike during the protests.


Indian writer and artist Shuddhabrata Sengupta points out that the movement is not the first major “Gen Z”-led protest in the country. Six years ago, India’s streets exploded in protest of the Citizenship Amendment Act, which purported to provide asylum seekers from religious minority groups a path to citizenship, but excluded Muslims, who face severe levels of persecution under the BJP’s Hindu nationalist government. “There’s clearly a restlessness for change and an unwillingness to accept the lies and the slander that the regime produces on a daily and a nightly basis,” says Sengupta.

title: [Portugal] Lançamento: “A Felicidade de Todos os Seres na Sociedade Futura”, de António Gonçalves Correia
content:
Publicado originalmente em 1922, 

A Felicidade de Todos os Seres na Sociedade Futura

 é uma reflexão visionária de António Gonçalves Correia sobre a construção de uma sociedade baseada na igualdade, na cooperação e na liberdade.


Partindo de uma crítica profunda ao capitalismo, à propriedade privada e às injustiças sociais, o autor imagina um futuro onde o trabalho, a educação, a cultura e os recursos são partilhados em benefício de todos os seres. Entre a utopia libertária e o apelo à transformação social, esta obra recupera uma das vozes mais singulares do anarquismo português com uma inegável actualidade perante a fragmentação do presente.


Sobre o autor


António Gonçalves Correia (1886–1967) foi jornalista, escritor, activista social e uma das figuras mais originais do anarquismo português. Natural de Castro Verde, destacou-se pela defesa do cooperativismo, do vegetarianismo, do pacifismo, da emancipação das mulheres e da transformação social inspirada nos ideais libertários. Fundador de jornais e impulsionador de diversas iniciativas comunitárias, foi também o principal animador da célebre Comuna da Luz, experiência de vida colectiva criada no Alentejo durante a década de 1920.

author: A.N.A.
title: O que é ser conservador?
content:
Uma crítica ao conservadorismo, do ponto de vista anticiv

 

A imagem acima foi criada pelos conservadores brasileiros. Ela representa uma luta entre duas forças: a ordem (fundamentos sólidos, que levam à liberdade e prosperidade) e o caos (o acaso, que supostamente leva à escravidão e pobreza). Ela apresenta o representante da ordem como um homem branco engravatando segurando o mundo em suas mãos, uma imagem que remete ao controle humano sobre a natureza, o que é reforçado pelo símbolo da IA, a união entre razão e tecnologia, remetendo à tecnocracia. Até o uso da cor azul reforça isso. O azul está associado à estabilidade, confiança, segurança e autoridade. É uma cor associada tanto ao empresariado quanto ao governo e à polícia. É também uma cor que nós tendemos a opor ao vermelho.

 

O Brasil não surgiu como um projeto autônomo de organização política, mas como uma colônia de exploração servindo à expansão mercantil europeia. A colonização precisou construir uma narrativa moral que legitimasse a conquista, a escravização e a extração de riquezas. Essa narrativa foi a ideia de que os povos indígenas eram “selvagens” e precisavam ser civilizados.

 

Quando os europeus encontraram sociedades que viviam sem propriedade privada, sem cristianismo, sem monarquia e sem mercado, o choque cultural foi enorme. Essa diferença cultural foi rapidamente entendida como inferioridade moral. Era preciso convencer a própria Europa de que a conquista não era apenas economicamente vantajosa, mas eticamente necessária. A missão colonial passou a ser uma missão civilizatória.

 

Foucault mostrou que o poder não depende só da força, mas da produção de discursos que definem quem é considerado normal, racional e civilizado. Quijano apontou como a “colonialidade do poder” se reproduz mesmo depois do colonialismo formal, e permanece na estrutura política da sociedade. Fanon demonstrou como o colonialismo produz uma psicologia da inferioridade nos povos colonizados e uma permanente necessidade de imitar o colonizador. Mbembe mostra como o poder colonial decide quais vidas merecem proteção e quais podem ser descartadas.

 

No Brasil, a herança colonial é mantida pelo conservadorismo. Ele se apresenta como defensor da “civilização” contra a barbárie. Historicamente, essa barbárie recebeu o nome de indígena, negro, comunista, anarquista, ateu, maconheiro, feminista, gay, travesti e assim por diante. Os alvos mudam, mas a estrutura do discurso permanece a mesma: a preservação da ordem natural está sempre ameaçada por forças do caos.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Ottawa eyes fall rollout for Nutrition North reforms
content:
The federal government expects to unveil long-awaited reforms to Nutrition North Canada this fall, but Northern Affairs Minister Rebecca Chartrand says the changes will go beyond lowering grocery prices and will focus on building a broader northern food economy.


“When we look at reform, we know that a food subsidy alone will not solve the food insecurity issue,” Chartrand said in an interview.

“That is why we are looking at a whole government approach to address the food insecurity issues in the North.”


Established in 2011, Nutrition North provides subsidies and other support to help reduce the cost of nutritious food and essential items in 124 northern and remote communities, including in Nunavut and Nunavik.


The federal government

launched an external review

 of the program in October 2024, following years of criticism over whether the program was effectively reducing the high cost of groceries in the North.


That

review

, managed by f

ormer Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. president Aluki Kotierk, is one of many external and internal reports the department is

relying on

 to inform possible changes, Chartrand told Nunatsiaq News earlier this year.


The major focus of the reform will be shifting toward what Chartrand called a northern “food economy” — supporting food entrepreneurs, such as through the Harvester’s Support Grant, local supply chains, food processing and community-led solutions. 


Chartrand said reforms will be tailored to regional needs, as not every community equally relies on the Nutrition North subsidy to reduce food costs. 


“We don’t want to create sweeping changes that would pull the rug out from underneath people when we have heard that some communities rely on that subsidy,” she said. 


The government is also reviewing whether additional northern communities should become eligible for Nutrition North support.


The minister said the government’s review also examined concerns raised following a 2024 joint APTN and CBC News investigation that alleged some retailers were not fully passing Nutrition North subsidies on to consumers.


Chartrand said retailers told the government that the subsidy has not kept pace with inflation,

meaning the amount of support provided has not increased enough to match rising costs.


The federal government announced a $30-million top-up to Nutrition North in February to provide immediate support by subsidizing shipping costs for perishable foods and essential items while broader reforms are developed.


Beyond the retail subsidy, Chartrand said future reforms could include funding food infrastructure, including hydroponics, vertical gardening, greenhouses, community freezers, local distribution networks and Indigenous-led food businesses.


The successes of future reforms will be based on whether nutritious food becomes more affordable, whether access to country food improves, whether community-led food programs expand and whether northern food businesses grow, she said. 


Chartrand acknowledged northerners are frustrated after years of discussion without visible changes to grocery prices.


“We’re modernizing the retail subsidy, improving transparency and retailer accountability, expanding support for the harvesters and the country food program, looking to invest in community food infrastructure and entrepreneurship,” Chartrand said.


“T

hese steps, obviously, will take some time.”

title: "Tipping Point": Ex-CDC Official Links Cyclospora & Measles Outbreaks to Trump's Public Health Cuts
content:
The United States is facing a number of major disease outbreaks, from foodborne cyclosporiasis to vaccine-preventable measles. We speak to the former chief medical officer at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (

CDC

), Debra Houry. She resigned from her post one year ago in protest over political interference at the agency and the leadership of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., an anti-vaccine activist who has overseen the slashing of billions of dollars in public health funding during the second Trump administration.


“The U.S. is really at a tipping point, when you look at measles, whooping cough, all these vaccine-preventable diseases, as well, and the secretary is responsible for this,” says Houry. “Public health matters. When it works, you often don’t know, because you’re saving lives. But when you take it away, we see those consequences today.”

author: David Odhiambo
title: Portfolio Diplomacy: Rethinking African Economic Statecraft in a Multipolar World
content:
Walk through Nairobi and the twenty-first century global economy comes into view.


Chinese-built expressways carry commuters to office towers occupied by American technology firms. French retailer Carrefour has become one of the country’s largest supermarket chains. Japanese vehicles dominate the roads while Indian pharmaceutical companies supply hospitals and pharmacies. Increasingly, Gulf investors are financing the logistics corridors that connect Kenya to regional markets. None of these relationships is unusual on its own. Most people experience them as disconnected features of everyday life.


The Nairobi Expressway approaching Westlands. The GTC Complex, one of Nairobi’s tallest commercial developments, is visible in the background.


Yet, this is rarely the lens through which Kenya’s foreign policy is viewed. Public debate has instead become dominated by President Ruto’s extensive international travel. To supporters, those journeys reflect energetic economic diplomacy. To critics, they have become shorthand for a presidency more comfortable abroad than confronting rising taxes, public debt and domestic discontent at home.

Both perspectives, however, overlook a more important shift

.

 The debate has focused on where Kenya’s president travels rather than where Kenya’s economy is connected.


That distinction matters because the international economy that shaped African diplomacy over the past three decades is rapidly changing.


The End of the Old Development Model


For much of the post-Cold War period, African governments operated within a relatively stable political economy of development finance

.

 External capital flowed through a relatively small number of actors: Western bilateral donors, multilateral development banks and, from the early 2000s, increasingly Chinese policy banks. Diplomatic success largely meant securing access within that ecosystem.


That ecosystem is now fragmenting.

 The retrenchment of traditional development assistance provides perhaps the clearest illustration. According to the

OECD

, net official development assistance fell by 23.3 per cent in 2025 (the largest annual contraction on record) following an 8.5 per cent decline in 2024. Further reductions are projected for 2026, making this only the second time on record that ODA has declined for three consecutive years, after the period between 1992 and 1995. It’s the first time since that period that the United States, United Kingdom, Germany and France have all cut aid simultaneously.


Unsurprisingly, the sharpest reductions are expected to fall on low-income countries, with bilateral aid to sub-Saharan Africa projected to decline by as much as 28 per cent. The implication is not merely fiscal, the shrinking of aid budgets. It is structural. One of the central pillars of the post-Cold War political economy of development is becoming progressively less reliable.


A More Competitive Marketplace for Capital


Aid is only one pillar of a broader transformation.


China’s role has also evolved. The era of rapidly expanding policy-bank lending for large-scale infrastructure has given way to a more selective approach, with greater emphasis on debt sustainability, commercial viability and strategically targeted investment. Yet, this is not simply a story of one source of finance retreating. It is a story of many others emerging.


Gulf sovereign wealth funds have become increasingly important investors in ports, logistics, renewable energy and digital infrastructure. According to the

Africa Center for Strategic Studies

, the United Arab Emirates alone has announced around US$47 billion in projects across East Africa, with Saudi Arabia committing a further US$15.6 billion. Climate finance and private capital are also playing an increasingly prominent role in financing Africa’s development.


The result is a profound shift in the political economy of development: governments no longer navigate a relatively small ecosystem of donors and development banks. Instead, they operate within an increasingly competitive marketplace of capital that includes bilateral partners, sovereign wealth funds, institutional investors, multinational corporations and regional markets. In that ecosystem, diplomatic success may no longer be measured simply by how much capital a country attracts, but by how successfully it diversifies the sources from which that capital is drawn.


A Different Model of Integration

title: [Grécia] Iniciativa de Solidariedade com Nikos Maziotis e Pola Roupa
content:
A companheira Pola Roupa e o companheiro Nikos Maziotis foram condenados a 20 anos de prisão por sua participação na organização guerrilheira urbana anarquista Luta Revolucionária (Epanastatikós Agónas, ativa entre 2003 e 2017) sob o Artigo 187A do Código Penal Grego (a legislação antiterrorismo da Grécia). Ambos assumiram a responsabilidade política pela organização logo após suas prisões em abril de 2010.

 

Hoje, 16 anos após a repressão inicial contra a Luta Revolucionária, o companheiro Nikos permanece prisioneiro nos cárceres da “democracia”. Embora já tenha cumprido quatro quintos de sua pena (desde novembro de 2024), ele continua a ser submetido a um regime de exceção: ele é o primeiro prisioneiro político (sem prisão perpétua) a permanecer encarcerado apesar de ter cumprido todos os requisitos legais para a liberdade condicional há três anos. Isso não é mera coincidência. Ele é submetido a esse tratamento de exceção devido à sua postura firme e digna: ele não renega suas convicções, não faz declarações de remorso ou retratação, não desmerece suas ações ou a história da Luta Revolucionária e não faz concessões — afirmando a todos: os revolucionários não são “reeducados” nem “moralmente reformados”.

 

Além disso, o Estado também está se vingando da companheira Pola ao impor uma penalidade financeira efetivamente perpétua — uma medida tomada por razões políticas e impulsionada por motivações claramente políticas. A dívida financeira devida ao Estado — decorrente de multas e custas judiciais — atingiu um valor exorbitante, totalizando 45.000 euros. Ao mesmo tempo, ela está proibida de acessar ou usar qualquer uma de suas próprias propriedades. Tudo isso resulta em uma situação em que ela é mantida como refém perpétua — uma colonização de sua existência por meio da dívida, uma estratégia organizada de esganadura econômica projetada para levar, em última análise, à prisão.

 

Estamos lançando esta iniciativa para fornecer apoio político e material ao nosso companheiro anarquista Nikos Maziotis, que permanece aprisionado dentro do sistema penal do Estado democrático grego. Também nos solidarizamos com nossa companheira Pola Roupa, que continua sujeita a medidas restritivas até 2030, além de arcar com as dívidas esmagadoras que lhe foram impostas.

 

Para fazer contribuições financeiras ou oferecer solidariedade, você pode fazê-lo através do Borrokan ou diretamente através da Assembleia de Apoio a Nikos e Pola, sediada em Atenas:

title: Sobre alguns camaradas perseguidos e presos nos últimos dias na Grécia
content:
TIREM AS MÃOS DOS NOSSOS 3 CAMARADAS


Nos últimos dias estamos vivendo uma situação de disseminação do medo criada pelo governo e promovida pela mídia, por ocasião dos ataques incendiários em Tessalônica, da instrumentalização da morte de uma mulher e da reabertura do caso MARFIN após dezesseis anos. O alvo é o espaço anarquista, com narrativas do tipo: “alguém começa com travessuras e tinta, passa para pedras e coquetéis molotov e termina com bombas e pistolas”.


16 anos depois, o Estado traz o caso Marfin de volta ao centro das atenções midiáticas e repressivas. Uma história que a ND (Nova Democracia) evoca constantemente numa tentativa de criminalizar as enormes e intensamente conflituosas mobilizações que ocorriam na época contra as medidas de austeridade, que buscavam colocar o peso do custo da crise econômica sobre os ombros dos de baixo.


16 anos depois, o alvo conveniente sobre o qual o governo tenta deslocar sua agenda pré-eleitoral para campos mais úteis a ele é, mais uma vez, o espaço anarquista e, mais especificamente, quatro camaradas cujas casas foram invadidas; dois deles foram presos. As “provas” que apareceram na mídia até agora batem recordes de ridículo. Das ligações telefônicas anônimas às quais infelizmente já nos acostumamos, passamos para e-mails anônimos, o que também combina com os tempos atuais. Softwares de IA foram mobilizados após 16 anos para comparar fotos de… férias mostrando roupas semelhantes.


16 anos depois, os problemas continuam os mesmos. Diante das políticas estatais de morte, que tornaram a vida cotidiana insuportável; da tentativa de execução de um homem por fugir de uma barreira policial; dos trabalhadores assassinados em campos de trabalho por todo o país; e das operações de guerra que banham populações em sangue ao redor do mundo, a resposta é luta, perseverança, conflito. E o espaço anarquista esteve e estará presente nisso, com todos os meios.


Solidariedade aos processados no caso Marfin


ESTADOS E CAPITAL SÃO ASSASSINOS E TERRORISTAS


Anarquistas e camaradas dos acusados em mais uma conspiração estatal


*****


Nesta manhã, 11/7, a organização criminosa Estado lançou um 

pogrom

 coordenado contra o espaço anarquista em Chania, em Creta, Atenas e Tessalônica. Camaradas foram perseguidos e prisões foram realizadas. Este novo e mais sofisticado episódio de repressão é uma tentativa desesperada da gangue governante de reverter o clima de indignação social contra ela.


Hoje houve uma tentativa de lançar uma sombra sobre o assassinato, por dezenas de policiais descarados, de um jovem de vinte anos atingido com 13 tiros nas costas enquanto corria para salvar a própria vida; assim como de encobrir o caso de policiais que estupraram uma menina de onze anos na Delegacia de Omonia. Dois acontecimentos que revelam a natureza de um governo de assassinos e estupradores. Responsável pelo afogamento de milhares de imigrantes, pelo massacre de centenas de trabalhadores em fábricas e zonas industriais, como ocorreu hoje em Aspropyrgos. Capital e governo enriquecem às custas de um povo que se torna cada dia mais descartável. Estão trabalhando intensamente para inverter esse clima, de modo que os assassinos apareçam como vítimas, e o caminho é bem conhecido.


Perseguir e prender sem provas, para criar impressões. Mas jogos políticos com nossas vidas não terão sucesso tão facilmente. Nesse clima, nossas casas foram invadidas esta manhã sem qualquer justificativa, e material digital como celulares, computadores e mídias de armazenamento foi roubado. Nem sequer tiveram a “gentileza” de nos dizer se as invasões de nossas casas estavam relacionadas a algum caso específico, ou o que exatamente procuram. O que resta é uma ameaça permanente e nossa situação de reféns, bem como uma lição para nossas crianças, que vivenciaram tudo isso, sobre o que é a gangue criminosa do Estado.


Os colaboradores do genocídio do povo palestino, e seus lacaios, os jornalistas, não têm direito de falar em justiça. Nós temos todo o direito de falar em vida.


Recuem, delatores; avancem, camaradas


Viva a anarquia!


A.S., I.L.


PS:


Em 11/7/26, o Serviço Antiterrorismo e a Diretoria de Combate ao Crime Organizado realizaram operações em Atenas, Tessalônica e Chania, em Creta, quase simultaneamente, durante as quais 5 camaradas foram presos, enquanto foi emitido um mandado para outra pessoa. Os 2 em Atenas foram acusados pelo incêndio do [banco] Marfin em 2010, e os 3 restantes pelo ataque incendiário …

title: U.N. Expert Francesca Albanese Slams U.S. "Complicity" as Trump Meets Netanyahu Despite ICC Warrant
content:
We speak to Francesca Albanese, the United Nations special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, about Israel’s continued impunity from international law. Despite an International Criminal Court warrant out for his arrest, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recently visited the White House to meet with President Donald Trump. While the United States is not a member state to the

ICC

, “It doesn’t mean that they have to extend protection to a fugitive from international law,” says Albanese, who joins widespread international calls for Netanyahu’s arrest. “The United States is actively contributing to make the international criminal law architecture that it has been building, from the Nuremberg trials up until now, crumble on our head.”


Albanese also comments on settler- and soldier-led “pogroms” in the occupied West Bank and calls out the complicity of the governments of Greece, Italy and France, which, despite being party to the

ICC

, authorized Netanyahu’s travel through their airspaces. “It looks small in the context of a genocide, but every action matters, as every crime matters and will be accounted for,” she says.

author: Equality Now
title: What to know about human trafficking this World Day Against Trafficking in Persons
content:
29th July 2026


What to know about human trafficking this World Day Against Trafficking in Persons


6 min read


News and Insights


End sexual exploitation


Global


Human trafficking is a crime committed by criminal networks against vulnerable individuals. While traffickers and exploitative actors must be held accountable, trafficking is also a human rights issue rooted in inequality and failures in protection systems.


For

World Day Against Trafficking in Persons

, we explore what trafficking looks like, why it happens, and why ending it requires more than criminal prosecutions alone.


Human trafficking is defined by exploitation, not movement


Human trafficking is often associated with the notion that people need to be moved across borders to be considered trafficked. But under international law, trafficking is defined by exploitation, not movement.


The

Palermo Protocol

 defines trafficking as the recruitment, transportation, transfer, harbouring, or receipt of people through threats or use of force, coercion, deception, abuse of a position of vulnerability, or other prohibited means for the purpose of exploitation. A person can be trafficked within their own community, country, or region. What matters is not where someone is taken, but whether they were exploited.


Trafficking takes many forms


When a human is trafficked, it can be for many reasons, and it can look different depending on the situation. Trafficking can be for sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, or forced criminality, among other things. Often these forms of exploitation are interconnected, and many survivors have experienced multiple forms of exploitation once trafficked.


While people of all genders can experience trafficking, women and girls are disproportionately affected by trafficking for sexual exploitation. Sex trafficking also exists within a broader continuum of gender-based violence, where inequality, discrimination, and harmful social norms can increase vulnerability to exploitation.


Traffickers exploit inequality


Trafficking is interconnected with a broader continuum of gender-based violence and exploitation. Traffickers exploit existing vulnerabilities created by inequality and lack of protection. Often, by the time a woman or girl is trafficked, countless opportunities to prevent it have already been missed.


Poverty, limited access to education, gender-based violence, discrimination, weak labour protections, and economic insecurity can all create conditions that traffickers manipulate.

Climate-related disasters

, conflict, and displacement can further increase risks by disrupting livelihoods and support systems.


While these factors do not cause trafficking, they create opportunities for traffickers to exploit. 


Technology is changing the way exploitation happens


Technology has presented new means for knowledge sharing, communication, and connection,  and if misused, it creates new tools for exploitation.


Traffickers increasingly use digital platforms to groom, recruit, manipulate, and exploit victims.

Emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, deepfake technology, and digitally generated sexual abuse material, are creating new forms of harm

 while legal protections and accountability mechanisms struggle to keep pace.


Addressing trafficking today requires understanding how exploitation evolves and ensuring that technology companies, governments, and policymakers take responsibility for preventing abuse.


Addressing trafficking as part of a broader human rights approach


At Equality Now, we work to strengthen laws and systems that can prevent trafficking and protect those at risk of exploitation. We use international law and standards to advance legal reform and implementation,

 pursue accountability through strategic litigation

, and advocate through international and regional human rights mechanisms. 


While

international standards recognise that governments must prevent trafficking, protect survivors, provide access to services

, prosecute traffickers, and address the conditions that allow exploitation to occur, no single law, institution, or sector can end trafficking alone. 


Governments must implement and enforce laws, while civil society, journalists, educators, labour actors, healthcare providers, technology companies, and international and regional human rights bodies all have a role in preventing exploitation and ensuring survivors can access …

title: Continúan las agresiones a comunidad Cueva del Inca y su gente
content:
La Comunidad Cueva del Inca viene sufriendo atropellos a sus derechos, desde hace tiempo. Por ejemplo, el año pasado en el mes de septiembre y luego de varios intentos de desalojos, con la presencia de policía e infantería, una patota por orden de Carlos Vasquez, empresario del hotel “Canto del Viento”, que ambiciona las tierras de la comunidad, ingresó al territorio, hostigando y amenazando a las mujeres.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Cueva-del-Inca-Tilcara.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Cueva-del-Inca-Tilcara.mp3


.Descargar audio


Luego, en este año, en el mes de junio las comuneras y comuneros se autoconvocaron en protesta frente al Concejo Deliberante de Tilcara en defensa de su autonomía para colocar nombres a sus propias calles, además de denunciar los intentos de despojos de su comunidad.  En esa oportunidad la intendenta Sonia Pérez fue quien anuló el proyecto de los nombres que se había aprobado ya.


Y en esta permanencia que hicieron los comuneros frente al Concejo, el indianista, comunicador y músico Gastón Cabana, fue demorado y de manera intimidatoria los efectivos procedieron a investigarlo.


Luego fue liberado tras ser notificado de la denuncia del empresario Vasquez con la causa armada de “lesiones” contra los manifestantes.


La comunidad expresó que “el hostigamiento policial se da en el marco de persecución a defensores de derechos territoriales buscando desmembrar la solidaridad y difusión”.


Así que, en esta oportunidad, vamos a escuchar al hermano Cabana, quien explica más detalladamente la situación que tuvo que soportar y su preocupación por la causa que le armaron.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense
